answer: Each identity must complete a fixed sequence of modular squarings, with every result feeding the next; a Wesolowski proof lets peers verify the delay efficiently, not skip its generation. GPUs can run separate identities in parallel, but cannot collapse one chain’s dependencies, so each clone still incurs the full time cost. This bottleneck makes Sybil attacks expensive, not impossible—a copper thread through the fable, not a guarantee of uniqueness.
